issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise product estimate (2.8) is false for general periodic Sobolev functions. For instance, taking $\alpha=2$ on $\Omega=[-\pi,\pi]^2$, where $(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2} = -\Delta$ and $C(2)=2$, choose smooth functions $f(\mathbf{x}) = \sin(x_1)$ and $g(\mathbf{x}) = -\sin(x_1)$. At $\mathbf{x}=0$, $f(0)=g(0)=0$, so the right-hand side is $0$, while $(-\Delta)(fg)(0) = (\sin^2(x_1))''(0) = 2\cos(0) = 2$, violating $2 \leq 0$. Moreover, in (3.9), the authors invalidly apply this pointwise inequality inside an $L^2$ inner product with signed functions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pointwise product estimate with standard fractional commutator estimates (such as the Kato-Ponce inequality) and establish the convective term bound directly via commutator bounds, restricting to $\alpha > 1$ or modifying the Sobolev energy framework to avoid embedding $H^2(\mathbb{T}^2)$ into $W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{T}^2)$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 2.2 is false as stated. Consequently, the energy estimate in Lemma 3.3 bounding the nonlinear convective term in the $H^{1+\alpha}$ norm is unsupported.
issues.title: False pointwise product inequality for the fractional Laplacian
issues.why_classification: Resolving this requires replacing the core nonlinear energy estimate with valid commutator estimates and adjusting the functional framework, and excludes or requires substantially different arguments for the endpoint $\alpha=1$ in two dimensions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}, we may repeatedly apply the local existence and uniqueness Lemma \ref{conv_lemma}. At each iteration step $t = k\bar{T}$, we take $u_N(k\bar{T})$ as the new initial data and solve forward on $[k\bar{T}, (k+1)\bar{T}]$. This bootstrap argument yields a solution that exists uniquely on any given  time interval $[0,T]$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.2 asserts global existence of strong solutions in $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}(\Omega)$ for all $T \geq 0$. However, Lemma 3.3 only proves a bound on a finite time interval $[0, \bar{T}]$ where $\bar{T} = 1/(C\|u_0\|_{1+\alpha})$ from the superlinear differential inequality $dD/dt \leq C D^{3/2}$, which exhibits finite-time blow-up. Remark 3.4 attempts to iterate this by claiming that (3.5) holds uniformly in time, which is circular because (3.5) was only established up to $t \leq \bar{T}$. Iterating this restart procedure with increasing initial norms causes the time steps to decay geometrically ($\sum \bar{T}_k < \infty$), which cannot cover arbitrary $T$ without an a priori global bound in $H^{1+\alpha}$.

failure_location.quote: Then there exists a unique solution $u \in L^\infty(0,T; H^{1+\alpha}_{\text{per}}(\Omega))$ of the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK} with  $\partial_t \bar{u} \in L^\infty(0,T; L^2_{\text{per}}(\Omega))$ for all $T\geq 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken Theorem 3.2 from a global-in-time existence result for all $T \geq 0$ to a local-in-time existence and uniqueness result valid on the finite interval $[0, \bar{T}]$ determined by the initial data norm.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that solutions exist globally in time for all $T \geq 0$ for arbitrary initial data $u_0 \in H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}(\Omega)$ is unestablished.
issues.title: Unjustified global-in-time existence via circular continuation of local ODE bound
issues.why_classification: The claim of global-in-time existence for all $T \ge 0$ must be abandoned in favor of a local existence result, representing a major reduction in the advertised temporal guarantee.
